author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: A source-only reset clears tok_a_q and tok_v_a_q while the consumer is active. The one-stage tok_b1_q takes the cleared token before the two-stage valid falls, so the consumer emits a zero token marked valid.

author_reading.rationale: The sender issues only while a ready level from the receiving domain is set, and ready rises only after the receiver's own reset releases, so no token is issued into a receiver still in reset.

labels.rationale: The sender issues tokens only while rdy is set by the receiver's reset-aware ready level. Both sides reset independently, but tokens are level-valid, so a one-sided reset drops in-flight tokens rather than creating spurious ones.

B can restart before its ready-low level has passed through the A synchroniser. A can keep valid asserted across the restart, allowing B to accept stale tokens before the sender has observed the reset.
labels.suspected_flaw: The ready dependence is one-way and does not meet the RDC-023 reciprocal trigger. The continuously changing payload has a separate containment defect.

settlement.rationale: B is right that the design is bad: the ready level orders release only, and does not protect the consumer from a producer reset. B places the hazard at the receiver restart, but the concrete corruption is the zero token produced by a producer-only reset, so the class is reset-domain data crossings (RDC-005). A and the author consider only the ready gating.
